text: I'll start by looking at the workspace layout and searching for CSV-related code.
The root cause is clear: line 18 of `library/csv_import.py` forcibly ASCII-encodes the input with `errors="ignore"`, which drops every non-ASCII character before parsing. The test run confirms it.

args.root_cause: parse_orders_csv() forcibly converts the entire CSV text to ASCII before parsing: `text.encode("ascii", errors="ignore").decode("ascii")`. The `errors="ignore"` option silently deletes every non-ASCII code point, so accented letters in customer names (e.g. "José Martínez" -> "Jos Martnez") are removed before csv.DictReader ever sees them. The line is unnecessary for parsing and is the sole cause of the data loss. The fix is to remove that line (or otherwise preserve Unicode, e.g. ensure the input is decoded correctly as UTF-8 upstream) rather than stripping non-ASCII characters.
